findings.description: `agent()` spreads `LOCAL.passEnv` after its protected `PATH`, allowing a `passEnv` entry for `PATH` to replace the path that puts sandbox wrappers first. If that entry is configured, an agent-authored test invoked through an allowed `node` or `npm` command runs on the host instead of in Docker.
findings.title: A config entry can bypass test isolation

citations.citation: The earlier sandbox fix established that agent-written tests must not run with host access.

evidence.explanation: The generated node/npm wrappers depend on BIN being first in PATH. The new spread can replace that PATH with the runner's host PATH, while the agent is allowed to run node and npm commands against files it writes in its worktree.

findings.description: `agentSettings()` spreads `settingsKeys` and `denyDirs` without checking their types, and the local JSON reader can also return `null`. A syntactically valid but malformed local file therefore throws during module initialization, before the runner's ticket error handler can record or report the failure.
findings.title: Invalid local settings crash the timer

evidence.explanation: The parser catches JSON syntax errors but accepts any parsed JSON value. The settings helper immediately spreads two optional fields outside the main lifecycle try block, which starts much later.

findings.description: The unit removes the previously configured tooling directory from its default PATH and makes the replacement environment file optional. If that file is absent on a machine where `claude` lives in the removed directory, the service starts Node but `agent()` fails to spawn `claude` when it picks up a ticket.
findings.title: Ticket runs cannot find the agent tool

citations.citation:
# node lives under the home directory, not in systemd's default PATH. A machine-specific PATH (for
# example where claude is installed) goes in the uncommitted ~/.config/qodo-agent/env, which overrides this
Environment=PATH=%h/.nvm/versions/node/v25.2.1/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
EnvironmentFile=-%h/.config/qodo-agent/env
# run the merged copy from origin/main, not whatever branch the working checkout is on
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/git -C %h/qodo-hack-2026 fetch -q origin main
ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c 'mkdir -p %h/.local/state/qodo-agent && for f in agent-watch.mjs runner-lib.mjs; do git -C %h/qodo-hack-2026 show origin/main:scripts/$f > %h/.local/state/qodo-agent/$f || exit 1; done'
ExecStart=%h/.nvm/versions/node/v25.2.1/bin/node %h/.local/state/qodo-agent/agent-watch.mjs

To let the factory pick up tickets (Linux, user systemd):
```sh
systemctl --user link ~/qodo-hack-2026/scripts/systemd/qodo-agent.service ~/qodo-hack-2026/scripts/systemd/qodo-agent.timer
systemctl --user enable --now qodo-agent.timer
```
Then label a ticket `ready-for-agent`. Progress is in `~/.local/state/qodo-agent/events.log`.

evidence.explanation: The removed unit PATH included the tooling directory, while its replacement file is optional. The setup instructions do not create that file; the runner subsequently launches `claude` by name and treats a failed spawn as a stopped agent run.

findings.description: `agentSettings()` copies every user-settings key named by `local.settingsKeys`, although the generated settings are meant to exclude user hooks and other control settings. If a local file names `hooks` or another non-sign-in key, those user settings enter the unattended Claude invocation instead of being filtered out.
findings.title: Local keys can enable user hooks

evidence.explanation: The helper copies any locally named key found in user settings and only overwrites `permissions` afterward. Its own comment promises that hooks, plugins and MCP are excluded, but the test exercises only a benign added key.

findings.description: The local-config reader silently substitutes `{}` on a missing or unreadable file, while `agentSettings()` no longer retains the former sign-in key by default and `agent()` no longer forwards the former region variable by default. On a machine that has not been provisioned with both local lists, the runner proceeds to launch Claude without values the previous invocation supplied.
